# Dodgers return to NLCS as Pages delivers clutch October moment
October 8th, 2026
Sonja Chen
ATLANTA -- Coming off a historically poor offensive performance last postseason, Andy Pages went hitless through the first two games of this year's NL Division Series. The small sample of seven at-bats raised some concerns, especially because he missed most of the final month of the regular season due to a fracture in his left hand.
Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged that Pages' performance was some cause for concern. But before the series shifted to Atlanta, Roberts reaffirmed his trust in the young center fielder, a first-time All-Star who became an integral piece of the Dodgers' lineup this season.
"I believe in him," Roberts said. "I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we're gonna need him to be an active part of our team."
Roberts' faith was rewarded when Pages came through with a two-run single in the seventh inning of NLDS Game 4 on Wednesday night at Truist Park, driving in the winning runs of the Dodgers' 4-1 victory over the Braves that punched their ticket to a third straight NLCS appearance.
"I like being in those at-bats," Pages said in Spanish. "There are times the result comes, sometimes not. But I prepare to be in those spots, and today I was able to get the result."
Said president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman: "My favorite players [are] the ones where you just keep ripping up the sheet in terms of what the strengths are, what the goals are, and they just keep exceeding expectations. And Andy has definitely been that."
The Dodgers have won their past five road postseason games dating back to Game 2 of the 2025 World Series, tying a franchise record. They are 10-1 in their past 11 road postseason games and 14-3 in their past 17. Game 1 of the NLCS is scheduled for Sunday at American Family Field in Milwaukee after the Brewers beat the Padres, 3-1, to clinch their NLDS on Wednesday night.
Bidding for the fifth three-peat in World Series history, the Dodgers have advanced to the next stage in their title defense. Three wins down, and eight to go if they are to reach their ultimate goal.
Pages' breakthrough single was the Dodgers' first -- and only -- hit in 20 plate appearances with runners in scoring position in the NLDS. In all best-of-five or longer postseason series, no team has had no hits in such situations and still won the series.
Last year, Pages' .211 OPS was the worst by any player who had taken at least 50 plate appearances in a single postseason. The poor performance led to him being benched from the starting lineup starting in Game 5 of the World Series, although he made a game-saving catch in Game 7 as a defensive replacement.
Pages used last year as fuel for his breakout 2026. And though he wasn't a big factor at the plate in the first three games of the NLDS, he announced himself with authority in Game 4.
"In this sport, you can't carry previous postseasons into this postseason. Everything is a new chapter," Kiké Hernández said. "Every time you take the field in October, you get an opportunity to rewrite your story."
Atlanta starter Tyler Mahle had been in a groove since the Dodgers tied the game with the help of two Braves errors in the second inning, but his outing came to an end after giving up a single to Teoscar Hernández with one out in the seventh. Righty reliever Didier Fuentes, who had stymied L.A. for 3 2/3 innings in Game 2, got the second out but issued consecutive walks to load the bases.
Right-hander Robert Suarez came on to face Pages, who worked a full count before getting a fastball he could work with. He punched a base hit into left-center, breaking the tie for good.
"You tip your cap to Pages, man," Braves manager Walt Weiss said. "He hit a 100 mph heater back through the middle."

# Dodgers beat Braves 4-1 to clinch NL Division Series after Pages’ go-ahead single in the 7th

The Dodgers advanced to the National League Championship Series as they seek to become the first NL team to win three straight World Series.

 Los Angeles center fielder Andy Pages hits a two-run single during the NLDS Game 4 between the Dodgers and the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday. Rich von Biberstein / Icon Sportswire via Getty

Oct. 8, 2026, 12:02 AM EDT / Source: The Associated Press

By The Associated Press

ATLANTA — Andy Pages drove in two runs with a bases-loaded single in the seventh inning to give Los Angeles the lead, and the Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 4-1 on Wednesday night to clinch their NL Division Series.

The Dodgers won back-to-back games in Atlanta to take the best-of-five matchup 3-1 and advance to the National League Championship Series as they seek to become the first NL team to win three straight World Series.

Pages lined a 3-2 pitch from Robert Suarez up the middle to drive in Teoscar Hernández, who singled off starter Tyler Mahle, and pinch-runner Tommy Edman for a 3-1 lead. Didier Fuentes walked pinch-hitter Josue De Paula and Kyle Tucker to load the bases. Edman ran for De Paula.

Max Muncy’s solo shot off Raisel Iglesias in the ninth padded the lead and gave the slugger 19 postseason homers with the Dodgers, extending his franchise record.

Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow, making his first start since Sept. 24, allowed only one hit but walked five batters in 4 2/3 innings. After he issued two walks in the fifth, left-hander Alex Vesia ended the inning on Matt Olson’s groundout to second base.

The missed opportunity left the Braves with 18 walks in the series, and none scored.

Glasnow and four relievers combined to give up just three hits. Tanner Scott pitched a perfect eighth before Edwin Díaz got three quick outs for the save.

Mahle, a native of Newport Beach, California, who grew up a Dodgers fan, allowed two runs — one earned — in 6 1/3 innings.

Michael Harris II hit Glasnow’s first pitch for a single before stealing second and eventually scoring from third on a wild pitch that bounced off catcher Will Smith’s chest protector.

The Dodgers pulled even in the second with the help of two Atlanta errors. Shohei Ohtani walked, stole second and advanced to third on catcher Sean Murphy’s errant throw into center field. Muncy’s pop fly into shallow left field was dropped by shortstop Mauricio Dubón for another error, allowing Ohtani to score.

Hernández crashed into the wall while attempting to catch Ozzie Albies’ double off Vesia leading off the sixth. Hernández pointed to his head and neck when talking to an athletic trainer but remained in the game.

Edgardo Henriquez stranded Albies at second. Henriquez allowed one hit in 1 2/3 scoreless innings for the win.

## Injury report

Dodgers second baseman Miguel Rojas was held out after leaving Tuesday night’s 3-1 win during an at-bat in the eighth inning with lower back soreness. Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts said Rojas would not be available off the bench.

Ronald Acuña Jr. started in right field for Atlanta one day after being moved to designated hitter in a late lineup change due to right knee soreness.

The Dodgers will face Milwaukee or San Diego in Game 1 of the NLCS on Sunday.

# Dodgers Beat Braves in NLDS, Advance to NLCS for Third Straight Year 

The Dodgers are back in the NLCS.

Noah Camras|

Oct 7, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman (5) reacts with Atlanta Braves third baseman Austin Riley (27) during the third inning in game four of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

In this story:

The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves, 4-1, in Game 4 of the National League Division Series, and have advanced to the NL Championship Series for the third consecutive season.

The Dodgers will play the winner of the Milwaukee Brewers vs. San Diego Padres NLDS. The Dodgers swept the Brewers in last year's NLCS.

## Dodgers vs Braves NLDS Game 4 Recap

Runs were hard to come by on Wednesday in Atlanta, as they've been for the entire series.

The Braves manufactured a run in the bottom of the first inning after Michael Harris II hit a leadoff single, stole second, advanced to third on a ground out and scored on a wild pitch.

That, however, wound up being Atlanta's lone run of the game.

The Dodgers quickly tied things up in the top of the second inning as Shohei Ohtani drew a leadoff walk, stole second and advanced to third on a throwing error. He then scored on a fielding error by Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubon.

> Shohei Ohtani makes his way around the bases to tie it! pic.twitter.com/8svHwvjK5T
> 
> — MLB (@MLB) October 7, 2026

Both pitchers settled in after that, and it wasn't until the bottom of the fifth inning when the Braves put another runner in scoring position.

After Tyler Glasnow walked two batters, he was relieved by Alex Vesia, who got Matt Olson to ground out to end the inning.

In the bottom of the sixth inning, the Braves again got a runner in scoring position as Ozzie Albies hit a leadoff double. However, after getting an out, Vesia was relieved by Edgardo Henriquez, who retired the final two batters of the inning.

In the top of the seventh inning, the Dodgers finally got some traffic of their own.

Teoscar Hernandez hit a one-out single and Josue De Paula pinch-hit and drew a two-out walk. Then, after Kyle Tucker walked to load the bases, Andy Pages hit a two-run single to give the Dodgers their first lead of the night.

> Dave Roberts didn't want to bench Andy Pages after Game 2 amid his playoff struggles: "I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we're gonna need him to be an active part of our team." Safe to say Roberts' decision worked. pic.twitter.com/5eZfBAmVPh
> 
> — Noah Camras (@noahcamras) October 8, 2026

In the bottom of the seventh inning, a two-out double by Harris put a runner in scoring position for the third straight frame. However, Henriquez got Ronald Acuna Jr. to ground out, maintaining the Dodgers' 3-1 lead.

Tanner Scott pitched the bottom of the eighth inning and retired the Braves in order in dominant fashion.

> Tanner Scott had a dominant bottom of the eighth inning to retire the Braves' 3-4-5 hitters. He punctuated it with this painted fastball that took the Braves' final ABS challenge. The Dodgers are three outs away from their third straight NLCS. pic.twitter.com/eEgFSYSEVs
> 
> — Noah Camras (@noahcamras) October 8, 2026

In the top of the ninth inning, Max Muncy gave the Dodgers an insurance run with a home run.

> Max Muncy gave the Dodgers an insurance run. He crushed a home run — the 19th of his postseason career — and Edwin Diaz will now have a three-run lead to protect in the 9th inning. Muncy is so, so good. pic.twitter.com/97lysp3jMR
> 
> — Noah Camras (@noahcamras) October 8, 2026

Then, Edwin Diaz entered for the save, and sent the Dodgers to the NLCS.

# Tarik Skubal dominates in 100-degree heat as the Dodgers beat the Braves 5-3 in NLDS opener

By AP

Updated: Oct 3, 2026, 08:07 pm

LOS ANGELES -- — Tarik Skubal tossed six dominant innings in triple-digit heat, Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Max Muncy homered, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 5-3 in Game 1 of their NL Division Series on Saturday.

 The game-time temperature of 100 degrees (38 Celsius) fell just short of equaling the Dodger Stadium record of 103 degrees at Game 1 of the 2017 World Series. The feels-like temperature was 105 degrees, with umpires chugging water between innings and fans shielding their heads with giveaway towels on a cloudless day.

 Skubal was cool, though. 

 The two-time Cy Young Award winner allowed one run and two hits, struck out seven and walked two while starting a postseason game at home for the first time in his career. His previous playoff starts were all on the road for the Detroit Tigers, who traded him to the two-time defending World Series champions just before the Aug. 3 deadline.

 “To go through six in these conditions I thought was fantastic," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, “and I thought the bullpen did a fine job.”

 Skubal's 63 strikeouts are the second-most in a pitcher’s first seven postseason appearances behind Bob Gibson’s 74.

 “It was a ton of fun,” Skubal said. “I've got a lot of respect for the fans that came out and showed up today. It’s not easy. It’s 100 degrees. The sun was on us the entire game.”

 Game 2 at Dodger Stadium is Sunday evening, when an extreme heat warning remains in effect.

 Hernández and Tucker both went through major slumps at the plate during the season. But they came up big with two-run homers against the Braves' bullpen. Atlanta's rotation got upended during its three-game NL Wild Card Series win over Philadelphia, with the Braves using ace Chris Sale in relief in the deciding game. 

 “We’ve been going through a lot this year, but we stayed together,” Hernández said. “We have each other’s back. We’re going to continue to try to do our best and try to do our job so we can keep winning.”

 Hernández and Tucker had nearly identical stat lines. Hernández went 2 for 4 with two runs and two RBI; Tucker finished 2 for 4 with a run and two RBI.

 Tucker had the worst regular season of his career after signing a $240 million, four-year deal with the Dodgers as a free agent. His offensive output sharply declined from his All-Star days with Houston and the Chicago Cubs. 

 Hernández stumbled through July and August before a swing fix sparked a September turnaround.

 “The bigger the moment,” Hernández said, “the more focused I get.”

 The Braves managed just four hits. Sean Murphy's two-strike, 421-foot homer leading off the sixth left them trailing 2-1.

 Ronald Acuña Jr. singled leading off the ninth against reliever Tanner Scott, who then served up a 432-foot homer to Ozzie Albies that cut the lead to 5-3. Scott got two outs before Evan Phillips induced a groundout by Austin Riley with a runner aboard to earn the save.

 Braves starter Dylan Dodd tossed three scoreless innings and gave up only singles to Shohei Ohtani in the first and Mookie Betts in the third. 

 The Dodgers broke through against Atlanta's bullpen in the fourth. Losing pitcher Victor Mederos walked Freddie Freeman before serving up Hernández's 431-foot shot to left-center, making it 2-0.

 Still bothered by nagging arm and knee issues, Ohtani batted second behind Betts. The four-time MVP lined to second with a runner on to end the third and flied out with a runner on in the fifth. 

 Tucker went deep in the sixth and Muncy added a solo shot off AJ Smith-Shawver two batters later, extending the lead to 5-1. 

Up next 

 The Braves did not announce a starter for Game 2 again

# Braves beat Dodgers, head home with NLDS tied at a game apiece

 4 hours, 15 minutes ago by BETH HARRIS / The Associated Press 

Atlanta Braves five-hole hitter Michael Harris II celebrates on third base after connecting for a triple in the top of the fifth inning during a playoff game Sunday against the Los Angeles Dodgers. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill)

LOS ANGELES — Michael Harris II tripled and scored the go-ahead run on reliever Kris Bubic's wild pitch in the fifth inning, and the Atlanta Braves beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 3-2 on Sunday night to even their National League Division Series at a game apiece.

"Getting the split in this place against these guys, yeah, it's awesome," Braves manager Walt Weiss said.

The best-of-five series shifts to Atlanta's Truist Park for the next two games Tuesday and Wednesday. The Braves swept a three-game series against the Dodgers there in late August after taking two of three in Los Angeles in early May.

Harris doubled to right field off reliever Edgardo Henriquez to drive in an insurance run with two outs in the top of the seventh in what turned into a bullpen game for both teams when the Braves chased Dodgers starter Blake Snell after 3 2/3 innings — his shortest postseason start since 2022, when he was still with the San Diego Padres.

Harris also singled in the third, coming up a home run short of hitting for the cycle. He also shined during third-seeded Atlanta's victories in the opener and the deciding third game of their NL wild-card series against the sixth-seeded Philadelphia Phillies this past week as the second-seeded Dodgers rested with a first-round bye.

"Michael had a great game," Weiss said of the 25-year-old center fielder who batted fifth in the lineup Sunday. "Postseason, you never know what's going to happen. There's no blueprint. There's no playbook. There seems to always be unsung heroes in the postseason."

Max Muncy's two-strike, two-out homer off Didier Fuentes pulled the Dodgers to 3-2 in the ninth. Braves closer Raisel Igelsias, their fifth reliever, earned his second save of the playoffs after getting pinch-hitter Josue De Paula to foul out to third to end the game.

"They're going to use any pitcher, try to get every matchup possible," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "They're going to ride certain guys, and obviously they use their bullpen accordingly."

Runs were hard to come by a day after the teams combined for five homers in the Dodgers' 5-3 victory to open the NLDS.

On Sunday, after Mookie Betts walked and Shohei Ohtani singled to open the bottom of the fifth, Atlanta's bullpen retired the next 14 hitters who went to the plate for the Dodgers.

Los Angeles stranded seven runners on base over the first five innings. Ohtani, a four-time league MVP, wasn't a factor for the second straight game, going 1-for-4 with two strikeouts.

"If you look at the at-bats, there's a lot of chase," Roberts said. "It's hard to square up, put good swings on balls that are out of the zone."

The Braves retook the lead, 2-1, on Bubic's wild pitch after Harris' two-out triple, his first ever in the postseason.

Freddie Freeman tied it at 1 on a two-strike solo shot off Braves reliever Grant Holmes in the fourth while facing his former team for the first time in the postseason.

"We've got to find a way to score some runs without hitting a home run. That's our biggest thing right now," said Freeman, a Southern California native who signed with the Dodgers in 2022 — a year after helping the Braves win the World Series in his 11th season with the only other MLB club he has played for.

"Get guys on base, get that big hit and hope that our pitching keeps doing good," added Freeman, who is trying to help the Dodgers win their straight World Series title.

Biggest Winners and Losers From Dodgers NLDS Win Over Braves

# Biggest Winners and Losers From Dodgers NLDS Win Over Braves

There are plenty of winners and a few losers from the Dodgers' NLDS win. 

Ricardo Sandoval|

Oct 7, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Left to right: Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto (18), pitcher Tarik Skubal (29), pitcher Blake Snell (7), and pitcher Tyler Glasnow (31), celebrate in the locker room after defeating the Atlanta Braves in game four of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

In this story:

The Los Angeles Dodgers are eight wins away from capturing their third consecutive World Series title after beating the Atlanta Braves in the National League Division Series.

The Dodgers are back in the NL Championship Series, where they're facing the Milwaukee Brewers in a rematch of last year's NLCS.

The Dodgers were the better team over the Braves from top to bottom, showing and proving to be a more explosive offense with lights-out pitching in the starting rotation and out of the bullpen.

Here are the biggest winners and losers for LA.

## Winners

Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto 

The starters for Games 1 and 3, Skubal and Yamamoto delivered and proved to be the clear aces for the Dodgers. 

In Skubal's first postseason start as a Dodger, the left-handed pitcher gave Los Angeles six innings while allowing one run on two hits with seven strikeouts in Game 1. He immediately justified the Dodgers' decision to line him up as their Game 1 starter after the first-round bye.

The addition of Skubal wasn't just for the regular season and to possibly secure him past the 2026 season, but for moments like these. And now, heading into the NLCS and longer series, Skubal will be huge for Los Angeles moving forward.

The same goes for Yamamoto, as the 28-year-old delivered like only he does in October. 

Yamamoto was stellar on Tuesday, outdueling Chris Sale (even if he humbly didn't think he did). The Japanese sensation threw seven innings of one-run ball with 10 strikeouts and only one walk. The 10 strikeouts were a postseason career-high.

When the stakes are highest, Yamamoto seems to shine the brightest. He's now proven that to be the case for three postseasons in a row. 

> Yoshinobu Yamamoto's last 5 postseason outings: 7 IP, 4 H, 1 ER, 10 K in NLDS Game 3 2.2 IP, 1 H, 0 ER, 1 K in World Series Game 7 6 IP, 5 H, 1 ER, 6 K in WS Game 6 9 IP, 4 H, 1 ER, 8 K in WS Game 2 9 IP, 3 H, 1 ER, 7 K in NLCS Game 2 He got the win in all five of these games. pic.twitter.com/wS5bordc64
> 
> — Noah Camras (@noahcamras) October 7, 2026

Andy Pages

It's been a struggle for Pages in his postseason career. However, Pages wasn't fazed, coming up clutch for the Dodgers and giving the team the lead in the seventh inning of Game 4 with a two-out, two-run single.

The Dodgers were 0-for-15 with runners in scoring position before Pages came through in the clutch. 

In four games this series, Pages hit .286 with a .905 OPS across 14 at-bats. That's plenty to build off of moving forward.

> Dave Roberts didn't want to bench Andy Pages after Game 2 amid his playoff struggles: "I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we're gonna need him to be an active part of our team." Safe to say Roberts' decision worked. pic.twitter.com/5eZfBAmVPh

Edwin Diaz

The Dodgers' $69 million man looked like a different pitcher from the regular season into October. 

He made his Dodgers postseason debut in Game 2, entering in the sixth and striking out two in a perfect inning while touching 100.8 mph. Then he got the ninth inning in Game 3 and recorded his first postseason save as a Dodger. On Wednesday night, he earned his second save to close out the series.
